requirements.title: Open a session
requirements.rationale: An agent needs one id to attribute its work and its token spend to before it starts working.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access to the workspace named by `workspace_slug` (a registered workspace or a task fork) sends POST /sessions with a valid body
criteria.action: store a session with `status` `active`, `started_at` the current time, the caller's `user_id` (null for the admin token) and `credential_type` (`admin_token`, `api_key` or `pat`), the given `run_id`, `node_id`, `archetype`, `model` and `metadata`, and the given `id` in lower case or a generated version 4 UUID when none was sent
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the session object: every member of the session object is present; `ended_at`, `duration_ms` and `error_message` are null; `cache_creation_input_tokens` is 0; `forks`, `changes` and `sandboxes` are empty arrays; every count and every token total is 0; `metadata` is the JSON value that was sent

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/create_test.go, a table over the callers {alice with an API key, alice with a PAT holding sessions:write, the admin token} and the bodies {only workspace_slug, every member with an upper-case id and metadata {"a":[1]}, workspace_slug naming a fork of demo}: r = POST /sessions; assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.status == 'active'; assert r.json.started_at == clock.Now() in whole seconds; assert r.json.user_id and r.json.credential_type match the caller; assert r.json.id is lower case and, when none was sent, a version 4 UUID; assert r.json.metadata deep-equals the value sent; assert all seventeen members are present

criteria.condition: the body of POST /sessions has no `workspace_slug` or one that is not a non-empty string, or, for a caller with write access, an `id` that is not a UUID in the 8-4-4-4-12 form, a `run_id` that does not match `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_` followed by six lower-case hexadecimal digits, or a `node_id`, `archetype` or `model` that is not a string or is longer than 255 characters
criteria.action: refuse the request and store no session
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` and a message that names the member; the number of stored sessions is unchanged

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/create_test.go, a table over the bodies {no workspace_slug, workspace_slug "", workspace_slug 7, id 'not-a-uuid', id without hyphens, run_id '2026-01-02', run_id '20260102_030405_ABCDEF', node_id of 256 characters, model 5, archetype of 256 characters}: r = POST /sessions as alice; assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert the message contains the member name; assert count(sessions) == 0. A 255-character node_id is accepted with 201

criteria.condition: POST /sessions is sent by a PAT without `sessions:write`, by a caller whose level on the named workspace is none, for a slug that names no workspace, by a bound token whose binding does not cover the slug, or by an org member with read-only access
criteria.action: refuse the request and store no session
criteria.contract: a PAT without `sessions:write`: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`, whether or not the workspace exists; level none, an unknown slug and an uncovered slug: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` and message `workspace not found`, with identical bodies apart from the request id; an org member: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden`

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
a coverage stub installed in the session component
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/create_test.go, a table {PAT of alice with only sessions:read -> 403 insufficient_scope; the same PAT naming slug 'nope' -> 403 insufficient_scope; carol on demo -> 404; alice on 'nope' -> 404; the admin token on 'nope' -> 404; alice with a token bound to workspace 'other' naming demo (coverage stub answers bound, not covered) -> 404; bob on demo -> 403 forbidden}: assert status and error_type; assert the 404 bodies of carol-on-demo and alice-on-nope are equal; assert count(sessions) == 0

criteria.condition: the named workspace has status `archived` and the request carries no `id` of an existing session
criteria.action: refuse the request and store no session
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_archived`; for an org member of the archived workspace the answer is HTTP 403 `forbidden` instead

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/create_test.go: set demo's status to archived; r = POST /sessions as alice; assert r.status == 409 and error_type == 'workspace_archived'; r = POST /sessions as bob; assert r.status == 403; assert count(sessions) == 0. A table over the statuses {pending, cloning, failed, ready}: POST as alice answers 201

criteria.condition: POST /sessions carries the `id` of a session that the same user (or, for an admin-token session, the admin token) created for the same workspace
criteria.action: answer with the stored session and change nothing, also when the other members of the body differ from the stored session, when the id is sent in another letter case and when the workspace has been archived since
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the stored session object, equal to the body the creating request received; `started_at`, `model` and `metadata` keep their stored values; the number of stored sessions is unchanged

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/create_test.go: s = POST /sessions as alice with id X, model 'm1'; advance the clock; r = POST /sessions as alice (a PAT this time) with id upper(X), model 'm2', metadata {"z":1}; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json equals the body of the first answer; assert r.json.model == 'm1'; assert count(sessions) == 1; archive demo and repeat: still 200. Same for two posts by the admin token

criteria.condition: POST /sessions carries an `id` that exists for another user, for the admin token when the caller is a user (or the reverse), or for another workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the stored session unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `conflict`; the stored session is unchanged and no second session exists

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/create_test.go, a table with a stored session X of alice on demo: {dave (owner of workspace `other`) posts id X for other; alice posts id X for a fork of demo; the admin token posts id X for demo}: assert status == 409 and error_type == 'conflict'; assert a replay of id X by alice for demo still answers 200 with the session as first stored; assert count(sessions) == 1

criteria.action: for any number of concurrent POST /sessions requests by one user for one workspace with one `id`, store exactly one session, answer exactly one of them 201 and every other one 200 with that session

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/create_test.go: start 16 goroutines that POST /sessions as alice with the same id against a real store file; collect statuses; assert count(201) == 1 and count(200) == 15; assert every body has the same started_at; assert count(sessions) == 1

requirements.title: Complete a session once
requirements.rationale: The outcome of a session must be set once and stay, however often a retrying agent repeats the call.

criteria.condition: the creator of an `active` session, or the admin token, sends POST /sessions/:id/complete with `status` `completed`, `failed` or `timeout`
criteria.action: set `status`, `ended_at` to the current time, `error_message`, `duration_ms` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` in one store transaction, storing for an absent `duration_ms` the milliseconds between `started_at` and `ended_at`, for an absent `error_message` null and for an absent `cache_creation_input_tokens` 0
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the updated session object

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/complete_test.go, a table over the bodies {status completed only; status failed with error_message 'boom', duration_ms 1234, cache_creation_input_tokens 7; status timeout with duration_ms 0}: open a session at T; advance the clock 90 s; r = POST complete; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.status == body.status; assert r.json.ended_at == T+90s; assert r.json.duration_ms == body.duration_ms, or 90000 when absent; assert error_message and cache_creation_input_tokens as sent or null and 0; assert GET /sessions/:id returns the same object

criteria.condition: POST /sessions/:id/complete with a valid body names a session whose status is `completed`, `failed`, `timeout` or `terminated`
criteria.action: answer with the stored session and change none of its members
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the session object as it was before the request

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/complete_test.go, a table over the stored statuses {completed, failed, timeout, terminated (set directly in the store by a test helper)}: before = GET /sessions/:id; advance the clock; r = POST complete with status failed, error_message 'late', duration_ms 5; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json == before

criteria.action: for any two or more concurrent completes of one `active` session, apply exactly one of them and answer every one of them 200

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/complete_test.go: open a session; start 8 goroutines, half posting status completed and half status failed with distinct error_message values, against a real store file; assert every status == 200; s = GET /sessions/:id; assert s.status in {completed, failed}; assert s.error_message is the one sent with the status that was stored; assert every response body equals s

criteria.condition: the `:id` of POST /sessions/:id/complete or POST /sessions/:id/usage is not a UUID, or the creator sends a complete whose `status` is missing or is not one of `completed`, `failed` and `timeout` (`terminated` and `active` included), whose `duration_ms` or `cache_creation_input_tokens` is negative or not an integer, or whose `error_message` is not a string
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the session unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; a following GET of the session shows `status` `active` and `ended_at` null

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/complete_test.go, a table {path id 'abc' on complete; path id 'abc' on usage; body {}; status 'terminated'; status 'active'; status 'done'; duration_ms -1; duration_ms 1.5; duration_ms '3'; cache_creation_input_tokens -1; error_message 4}: assert status == 400 and error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert GET /sessions/:id still has status 'active'

criteria.condition: POST /sessions/:id/complete or POST /sessions/:id/usage is sent by a caller who may read the session and is neither its creator nor the admin token, a user calling for a session the admin token opened included
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the session and its usage records unchanged, while accepting the same request from any credential of the creating user and from the admin token
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden`; the session's `status` and its number of usage records are unchanged. A PAT without `sessions:write` gets HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/complete_test.go, a table over both routes with a session of alice on demo: {bob (member, reads demo) -> 403 forbidden; alice's PAT with only sessions:read -> 403 insufficient_scope; alice's API key when the session was opened with her PAT -> 2xx; the admin token -> 2xx}; and with a session the admin token opened on demo: {alice (owner) -> 403 forbidden; the admin token -> 2xx}; after each 403 assert the session is 'active' and count(usage) == 0

criteria.condition: POST /sessions/:id/complete or POST /sessions/:id/usage names a session the caller may not read, a UUID that names no session, or, for a bound token, a session whose workspace the binding does not cover, also when the token's user created it
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` and message `session not found`; the body for an unreadable session equals the body for an unknown id apart from the request id

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
a coverage stub installed in the session component
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/complete_test.go, a table over both routes with a session X of alice on demo: {carol on X; alice on a random UUID; alice with a bound token not covering demo on X}: assert status == 404, error_type == 'not_found', message == 'session not found'; assert the bodies of carol-on-X and alice-on-random are equal; assert X is unchanged

requirements.title: Report and list token usage
requirements.rationale: Token spend is attributed by increments that an agent may send twice; a replay must never be counted twice.

criteria.condition: the creator of an `active` session, or the admin token, sends POST /sessions/:id/usage with a non-blank `model` of at most 255 characters and token counts that are integers of at least 0 or absent
criteria.action: store one usage record with the given `id` in lower case or a generated version 4 UUID, the session's id and `workspace_slug`, the model, the three counts with 0 for an absent one, and `reported_at` the current time
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the usage record {id, session_id, workspace_slug, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, reported_at}; the session's next GET shows the counts added to `token_summary` and the model in `models_used`

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/usage_test.go: open a session on demo; r1 = POST usage {model 'm2', input_tokens 10, output_tokens 5}; r2 = POST usage {model 'm1', cache_read_tokens 3, id upper(U)}; assert both status == 201; assert r1.json.cache_read_tokens == 0 and r1.json.workspace_slug == 'demo' and r1.json.reported_at == clock.Now(); assert r2.json.id == lower(U); s = GET /sessions/:id; assert s.token_summary == {total_input_tokens 10, total_output_tokens 5, total_cache_read_tokens 3, models_used ['m1','m2']}

criteria.condition: POST /sessions/:id/usage carries the `id` of a usage record that exists in the same session
criteria.action: answer with the stored record and store nothing, change no total and notify no usage observer, also when the replayed body differs from the stored record and when the session is no longer `active`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the stored usage record; the session's `token_summary`, its number of usage records and the number of observer notifications are unchanged

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/usage_test.go: register a counting usage observer; POST usage {id U, model 'm1', input_tokens 10} -> 201; r = POST usage {id U, model 'm9', input_tokens 999}; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.model == 'm1' and r.json.input_tokens == 10; assert count(usage) == 1; assert token_summary.total_input_tokens == 10; assert observer.calls == 1; complete the session and replay again: status == 200 and the same body

criteria.condition: POST /sessions/:id/usage carries a usage `id` that exists in another session
criteria.action: refuse the request and store nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `conflict`; neither session's `token_summary` changes

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/usage_test.go: open sessions A and B as alice; POST usage on A with id U -> 201; r = POST usage on B with id U; assert r.status == 409 and error_type == 'conflict'; assert B's token_summary totals are 0 and A's are unchanged

criteria.condition: POST /sessions/:id/usage with a new usage `id`, or none, names a session whose status is `completed`, `failed`, `timeout` or `terminated`
criteria.action: refuse the request and store nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `session_not_active`; the session's number of usage records is unchanged

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/usage_test.go, a table over the session statuses {completed, failed, timeout, terminated}: r = POST usage {model 'm1', input_tokens 1}; assert r.status == 409 and error_type == 'session_not_active'; assert count(usage of the session) == 0

criteria.condition: the creator sends POST /sessions/:id/usage whose `model` is missing, blank, not a string or longer than 255 characters, whose `id` is not a UUID, or one of whose token counts is negative or not an integer
criteria.action: refuse the request and store nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` and a message that names the member; the session's number of usage records is unchanged

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/usage_test.go, a table over the bodies {{}; model ''; model '   '; model 3; model of 256 characters; id 'x'; input_tokens -1; output_tokens 1.5; cache_read_tokens '2'}: assert status == 400 and error_type == 'invalid_request' and the message contains the member name; assert count(usage) == 0

criteria.condition: a new usage record has been committed
criteria.action: notify every registered usage observer exactly once with the record's workspace slug, model and three token counts, and notify none for a refused request
criteria.contract: each observer receives one call per stored usage record with (workspace_slug, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens); with no observer registered the request answers the same

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/usage_test.go: register two recording observers; POST usage {model 'm1', input_tokens 10, output_tokens 5, cache_read_tokens 3} -> 201; assert each observer recorded exactly [('demo','m1',10,5,3)]; POST a body with model '' -> 400 and a usage on a completed session -> 409; assert no further call; with no observer registered a POST still answers 201

criteria.condition: a caller who may read the session sends GET /sessions/:id/usage
criteria.action: answer the session's usage records ordered by (`reported_at`, `id`), descending by default and ascending with `order=asc`, paged by `limit` and `cursor`, together with `session_id` and `totals` computed over all records of the session regardless of the page
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {items, next_cursor, session_id, totals: {total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, total_cache_read_tokens, models_used}}; `items` is an array, empty for a session without usage; an `order` other than `asc` or `desc` is HTTP 400 `invalid_request`; an unreadable session is HTTP 404 `not_found` with message `session not found`

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/usage_test.go: store 5 usage records, two of them in the same second; p1 = GET usage?limit=2; assert len(p1.items) == 2 and p1.next_cursor != null; assert p1.totals sums all 5 records and p1.session_id is the session; follow next_cursor to the end and assert the 5 ids appear once each in (reported_at, id) descending order; GET usage?order=asc reverses it; GET usage?order=up -> 400; GET usage on a session without records -> items == [] and totals all 0 with models_used == []; carol -> 404; bob (member) -> 200

requirements.title: Read one session
requirements.rationale: The session is the thread a developer follows; who may read it must not depend on whether its fork still exists.

criteria.condition: GET /sessions/:id is sent by the session's creator with any credential of that user, by a caller with read access to the session's workspace, by a caller with read access to the parent of the task fork the session is on, or by the admin token
criteria.action: answer the session object, whatever the status of the workspace
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the session object, every member present

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/read_test.go, a table with session X of alice on demo and session Y of erin (a member of demo's org who created fork demo--t1) on demo--t1: {alice reads X; alice's PAT with only sessions:write reads X; bob (member) reads X; the admin token reads X; alice (owner of the parent) reads Y; bob reads Y; erin reads Y}: assert status == 200 and r.json.id; repeat the X rows with demo archived: still 200

criteria.condition: the workspace of a session no longer exists
criteria.action: keep the session readable by its creator and by the admin token and, when the workspace was a task fork, by every caller with read access to the fork's parent
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the session object for those callers, with `workspace_slug` the removed workspace's slug; HTTP 404 `not_found` for every other caller

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/read_test.go: open Y as alice on fork demo--t1 and Z as dave on workspace other; remove the records of demo--t1 and of other from the access component; assert GET Y as alice == 200, as bob (member of demo's org) == 200, as the admin token == 200, as carol == 404; assert GET Z as dave == 200, as the admin token == 200, as alice == 404

criteria.condition: GET /sessions/:id or GET /sessions/:id/usage names a session the caller may not read, a UUID that names no session, or, for a bound token, a session whose workspace the binding does not cover, also when the token's user created it
criteria.action: refuse the request without revealing whether the session exists
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` and message `session not found`; the body for an existing unreadable session equals the body for an unknown id apart from the request id

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
a coverage stub installed in the session component
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/read_test.go, a table over both routes with session X of alice on demo: {carol on X; carol on a random UUID; alice with a bound token whose coverage stub does not cover demo on X}: assert status == 404 and message == 'session not found'; assert the first two bodies are equal. A bound token of alice that covers demo reads X with 200

criteria.condition: the `:id` of GET /sessions/:id or GET /sessions/:id/usage is not a UUID, or the caller is a PAT holding neither `sessions:read` nor `sessions:write`
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: a malformed id: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; a PAT without either scope: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`, for an existing and for an unknown id alike

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/read_test.go, a table over both routes {alice with id 'abc' -> 400 invalid_request; alice with a 36-character id holding a 'g' -> 400; alice's PAT with only workspaces:read on an existing id -> 403 insufficient_scope; the same PAT on a random UUID -> 403 insufficient_scope; alice with the upper-case form of an existing id -> 200 with the lower-case id}

criteria.action: for any session response of any route (create, replay, complete, read, list), build `token_summary`, `forks`, `changes`, `sandboxes` and `counts` from the usage records and links stored at the time the response is built

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/read_test.go: open a session; a = GET it; POST usage {model 'm1', input_tokens 4}; record a fork link in a committed transaction; b = GET it; assert a.token_summary.total_input_tokens == 0 and b.token_summary.total_input_tokens == 4; assert a.counts.forks == 0 and b.counts.forks == 1; assert the session object returned by POST complete for the same id equals a following GET /sessions/:id

requirements.title: Record what belongs to a session
requirements.rationale: The packages that own forks, changes, pushes, commits, claims, lands and sandboxes need one way to say that a piece of work belongs to a session, so that the session record can show the whole thread.

criteria.condition: a calling package records a link (session id, kind `fork`, `sandbox`, `version`, `push`, `commit`, `claim` or `land`, workspace slug, key) inside a store transaction it owns, for a session that exists in any status
criteria.action: store the link in that transaction with the current time, so that it exists exactly when the caller's transaction commits
criteria.contract: the recording operation returns nil; after commit the session's next read counts the link; after a rollback the session's read is unchanged

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/link_test.go, a table over the seven kinds: tx = store.Begin(); err = Record(ctx, tx, Link{session, kind, 'demo', key}); assert err == nil; tx.Rollback(); assert counts of GET /sessions/:id are all 0; repeat with tx.Commit(); assert the count of that kind is 1. Repeat the commit case for a session that was completed first: the count grows from 0 to 1

requirements.title: List sessions
requirements.rationale: An operator or developer looks for the sessions of a workspace, a run or a period without knowing their ids.

criteria.condition: a caller sends GET /sessions
criteria.action: answer the sessions the caller may read (every session for the admin token; otherwise the sessions the caller created, the sessions of every workspace in the caller's readable set, and the sessions on task forks, removed ones included, whose parent is in that set), ordered by (`started_at`, `id`) descending by default and ascending with `order=asc`, paged by `limit` and `cursor`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {items: [session object…], next_cursor}; `items` is an empty array when nothing matches; no item is a session for which GET /sessions/:id would answer 404 to the same caller

requirements.title: Report the token cost of a workspace
requirements.rationale: An org member wants the token spend of a workspace per day, session or model over a window, without prices.

criteria.condition: a caller with read access to the workspace sends GET /workspaces/:slug/cost
criteria.action: sum the usage records whose `workspace_slug` is the slug and whose `reported_at` satisfies `since` ≤ `reported_at` < `until`, giving in `totals` the three token sums and the number of distinct sessions, applying no price, and counting no record of the workspace's task forks
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {workspace, period: {since, until}, group_by, totals: {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, sessions}, items: [{key, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, sessions}], next_cursor}; a record with `reported_at` equal to `since` is counted and one equal to `until` is not

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/session/cost_test.go: store usage on demo at T0 (session A: m1 10/1/0), T0+1h (session A: m2 5/0/2), T0+2h (session B: m1 7/7/7) and on fork demo--t1 at T0+1h (100/100/100); r = GET /workspaces/demo/cost?since=T0&until=T0+2h; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.totals == {input_tokens 15, output_tokens 1, cache_read_tokens 2, sessions 1}; with until=T0+3h totals == {22, 8, 9, sessions 2}; assert r.json.workspace == 'demo' and the JSON has no member other than the six named

criteria.condition: the request carries `group_by` `day`, `session` or `model`, or none
criteria.action: return one item per group ordered by `key` ascending, where `key` is the UTC calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD` of `reported_at` (`day`, the default), the session id (`session`) or the model name (`model`), each item with the three token sums and the number of distinct sessions of the group
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `group_by` echoing the effective value and `items` holding one entry per group; the sums of the items equal `totals` for the three token members

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token

criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `period.since` and `period.until` as RFC 3339 UTC timestamps of the effective window

setup: a hub handler built with httptest over a store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, and the access component seeded with users alice (owner of workspace `demo`), bob (member of demo's org), carol (no access) and the admin token

criteria.contract: HTTP 200; following `next_cursor` to the end returns every group exactly once in ascending key order; `totals` is identical on every page; `next_cursor` is null on the last page

requirements.title: Drive sessions from the command line
requirements.rationale: An agent in a shell reports its session with five commands instead of building HTTP requests.

criteria.contract: exit status 0 with the session object as one JSON document on stdout, for a 201 and for a 200 answer alike

execution_paths.title: An agent opens a session, reports usage and completes it

steps.action: sends POST /sessions with workspace_slug demo and prints the answer
checks write access to demo, stores an active session and answers 201 with the session object
runs `parley session usage <id> --model m1 --input 10 --output 5` and then `parley session complete <id>`
stores one usage record, then sets the session to completed with ended_at and duration_ms
runs `parley session get <id>` and reads status completed and total_input_tokens 10

real_components: the parleyd HTTP server with authentication and the access component
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a store in a temporary directory
a user with an API key who owns the ready workspace `demo`
end_state: `parley session get <id>` exits 0 and prints a session with status `completed`, a non-null `ended_at`, `token_summary.total_input_tokens` 10 and `token_summary.models_used` [`m1`]
a second `parley session complete <id> --status failed` exits 0 and the session still reads `completed`
`parley session usage <id> --model m1` now exits 1 with `error_type` `session_not_active` on stderr
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/session_test.go: hub = startHub(t); id = cli('session','start','demo','--model','m1').json.id; cli('session','usage',id,'--model','m1','--input','10','--output','5'); cli('session','complete',id); s = cli('session','get',id).json; assert s.status == 'completed' and s.token_summary.total_input_tokens == 10; assert cli('session','complete',id,'--status','failed').json.status == 'completed'; r = cli('session','usage',id,'--model','m1'); assert r.exit == 1 and r.stderr.error.error_type == 'session_not_active'

execution_paths.title: Work is linked to a session and a developer follows the thread and the cost

steps.action: opens a session on workspace demo with POST /sessions and reports usage on it
is asked by an operation on fork demo--t1 whether the agent may name the session, accepts the reference, and records a fork link and a version link in the operation's store transaction
reads GET /sessions/<id> as an org member of demo
builds the session object from the stored usage records and links and answers 200
answers the day's token sums for demo and the list holding the session

real_components: the parleyd HTTP server with authentication and the access component
the session component with its linking check and recording operation
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0
user alice owns workspace `demo` and its fork `demo--t1`; user bob is a member of demo's org
the test calls the linking check and the recording operation of the hub's session component directly, standing in for the fork and change packages
end_state: the linking check accepts alice's session for `demo--t1` and refuses it for bob with the unknown-session error
bob's GET /sessions/<id> shows `forks` [`demo--t1`], `changes` [{workspace `demo`, number 1}] and `counts` with forks 1, changes 1, versions 1
bob's GET /workspaces/demo/cost shows `totals.input_tokens` 10 and `totals.sessions` 1 with one item for the current UTC date
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/session_test.go: hub = startHub(t); id = post(alice,'/sessions',{workspace_slug:'demo'}).json.id; post(alice,'/sessions/'+id+'/usage',{model:'m1',input_tokens:10}); _, err = hub.Sessions.Check(ctx, aliceCaller, id, 'demo--t1'); assert err == nil; assert errors.Is(check(bobCaller, id, 'demo--t1'), session.ErrUnknownSession); hub.Store.Tx(func(tx){ hub.Sessions.Record(ctx, tx, forkLink(id,'demo--t1')); hub.Sessions.Record(ctx, tx, versionLink(id,'demo',1,1)) }); s = get(bob,'/sessions/'+id).json; assert s.forks == ['demo--t1'] and s.counts.versions == 1; c = get(bob,'/workspaces/demo/cost').json; assert c.totals.input_tokens == 10 and len(c.items) == 1; assert ids(get(bob,'/sessions?workspace=demo').json.items) contains id

execution_paths.title: A workspace change closes the workspace's active sessions

steps.action: opens two sessions on workspace demo and completes one of them
inside the store transaction of a workspace change, closes the active sessions of demo with reason `workspace archived` and writes one parley.session.force_closed event for the one it closed
answers the closed session as terminated with the reason and the completed session unchanged
reports usage on the terminated session and is refused with 409 session_not_active

real_components: the parleyd HTTP server with authentication and the access component
the session component with its closing operation
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0
user alice owns workspace `demo`; user bob is a member of demo's org
the test runs the closing operation of the hub's session component in a store transaction, standing in for the archive of package 14
end_state: the session that was active reads `status` `terminated`, `error_message` `workspace archived` and a non-null `ended_at`; the completed session is unchanged
the event log holds exactly one `parley.session.force_closed` event, with `resource_id` the terminated session's id and `metadata.reason` `workspace archived`
POST /sessions/<id>/usage on the terminated session answers 409 `session_not_active` and POST /sessions/<id>/complete answers 200 with status `terminated`
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/session_test.go: hub = startHub(t); a = open(alice,'demo'); b = open(alice,'demo'); post(alice,'/sessions/'+b+'/complete',{status:'completed'}); hub.Store.Tx(func(tx){ n, _ = hub.Sessions.CloseActive(ctx, tx, 'demo', 'workspace archived', now) }); assert n == 1; s = get(bob,'/sessions/'+a).json; assert s.status == 'terminated' and s.error_message == 'workspace archived'; assert get(bob,'/sessions/'+b).json.status == 'completed'; ev = events(hub, type='parley.session.force_closed'); assert len(ev) == 1 and ev[0].resource_id == a and ev[0].metadata.reason == 'workspace archived'; assert post(alice,'/sessions/'+a+'/usage',{model:'m1'}).status == 409; assert post(alice,'/sessions/'+a+'/complete',{status:'failed'}).json.status == 'terminated'
